SHEET General Info
1 2 MODEL FOR EVALUATION OF A NEW ROAD  PROJECT
3 2 Based on : S.Reutlinger, Techniques for project appraisal under uncertainty, World Bank 
4 2 Modified and extended by F.Plastria as case illustration to Software for Management, VUB
7 2 GENERAL AIM OF MODEL
9 2 Evaluation over a horizon of 20 years starting with construction period 
10 2 By means of simple cash flow analysis:
11 3 Net Present Value
12 3 Internal Rate of Return
13 3 Payback Period

SHEET Summary
1 2 GENERAL STRUCTURE OF THE MODEL
3 2 COSTS = Total construction costs new road
4 2                (evenly spread over construction period)
5 3 With additional cost and construction time when toll system is used
6 2 BENEFITS = Savings in  maintenance costs with new road vs. old road (=without new road)
7 2                     + possible income earned from tolls - operating cost toll
8 3 (all only to be calculated for the new road users)
9 2                     (exists only after start using new road)
11 2 CASH-FLOWS = BENEFITS - COSTS
13 2 Note: no taxes
15 2 Additional assumptions of the model
17 2 yearly estimations (over 20 years) for 
18 2 two types of vehicles: cars and trucks
19 2 Operating cost Toll system
20 3 Fixed part to keep system operational 24/7
21 3 Variable part (depends (linearly) on amount of traffic) per daily user
22 2 Maintenance costs
23 2 Separately for old and new road and types of vehicles
24 2 (Note: 'Old road' means "In case new road is not built", no fixed costs counted)
25 3 Fixed part per km (regularly preplanned maintenance, independent of traffic)
26 3 Variable part (depends (linearly) on amount of traffic) per km and user
27 2 Traffic estimation
28 2 Separately for types of vehicles
29 3 Global daily number of vehicle forecast: yearly %  increase
30 3 New road users: Part (=usage) of total depending on toll 
31 3 Each vehicle uses on average only part of the total roadlength
32 2 Toll effect
33 3 Very low price: no effect
34 3 Higher prices lead to lower usage (linear decrease)
35 3 Very high price: only price-insensitive users remain
37 2 Note: For formulas see the Model sheet
